question:
A magnetic material is placed in a magnetising field $H$. Its magnetisation is found to be in the direction opposite to $H$.
(i) Identify the type of material.
(ii) Explain the sign of its magnetic susceptibility.
(iii) State how its relative permeability compares with unity.

options.A:
(i) The material is ferromagnetic.
(ii) Its magnetic susceptibility is large and positive.
(iii) Its relative permeability is much greater than unity.
options.B:
(i) The material is paramagnetic.
(ii) Its susceptibility is positive because magnetisation is opposite to $H$.
(iii) Its relative permeability is less than unity.
options.C:
(i) The material is non-magnetic.
(ii) Its susceptibility is zero.
(iii) Its relative permeability is exactly unity.
options.D:
(i) The material is diamagnetic because its magnetisation is opposite to $H$.
(ii) From $M=\chi H$, $\chi$ is small and negative, $\chi<0$.
(iii) Since $\mu_r=1+\chi$, its relative permeability is slightly less than unity, $\mu_r<1$.
